payload.task_text:
I need help with a sf efficiency analysis. There is external benchmark data available that I need you to visit http://localhost:30334 and extract the relevant metrics.

Then pull our internal data from the company data warehouse for comparison.

Use the terminal to create and run a Python script called sf_efficiency_processor.py in the workspace that reads the collected data from JSON files you create, performs the analysis, and outputs sf_efficiency_results.json.

Create an Excel file called Hr_Dept_Efficiency_Report.xlsx with three sheets. The first sheet Data_Analysis should contain the main comparison data with relevant columns. The second sheet Metrics should summarize key metrics. The third sheet Recommendations should list actionable items.

The Data_Analysis sheet should include columns for the primary dimension, our internal metric values, the external benchmark values, and the gap or difference between them. Sort the data alphabetically by the primary dimension. The Metrics sheet should have two columns Metric and Value summarizing total counts, averages, and key statistics. The Recommendations sheet should list priority actions based on the gap analysis. Schedule a review meeting titled "Analysis Review" on March 14, 2026 from 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM UTC.

Use the department dimension for the comparison (one row per department), and name that first column exactly "Department". The Recommendations sheet must have two columns: "Priority" (the rank or priority level of each action) and "Action" (the recommended action text). Write all values into the Excel cells as literal numbers or text rather than spreadsheet formulas.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent. Read the benchmark at http://localhost:30334 and run the compact department warehouse aggregate concurrently, then create the required JSON inputs, sf_efficiency_processor.py, sf_efficiency_results.json, and Hr_Dept_Efficiency_Report.xlsx from one verified department join. Preserve the exact Department column, literal values, metrics, Priority/Action recommendations, and alphabetical rows; verify the files once and create or reuse the single specified UTC Analysis Review event.

nodes.text:
Plan this multi-system task: extract department-level external benchmark metrics from http://localhost:30334; query internal company warehouse for matching department metrics; create JSON inputs; create/run /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-pw-sf-hr-dept-efficiency-excel-gcal/workspace/sf_efficiency_processor.py producing sf_efficiency_results.json; build Hr_Dept_Efficiency_Report.xlsx with sheets Data_Analysis, Metrics, Recommendations and exact specified columns/literal values; create calendar event Analysis Review on 2026-03-14 14:00-15:00 UTC. Determine likely evidence sources, matching metric definitions, workflow dependencies, and validation checklist. Read-only planning only; do not modify anything. Return a concise executable plan.
Plan efficiency analysis

Visit http://localhost:30334 and extract the authoritative external benchmark data relevant to an SF efficiency analysis at department grain, one row per department. Capture exact department labels, metric names, values, units, reporting period (Q1 2026 if available), source/method notes, and any confidence indicators. Inspect rendered page and network/API responses as needed. Do not modify external state or local files. Return a structured table/JSON-ready payload plus source URL and extraction evidence. Acceptance: complete benchmark set needed to compare against company warehouse at department level, with no guessed values.
Extract benchmark metrics

Browser access to http://localhost:30334 failed because the configured browser is unavailable and install failed. Using read-only tools only, inspect available warehouse schemas/tables and local workspace artifacts to determine whether the authoritative external benchmark dataset is mirrored in Snowflake or files, and identify exact department-level KPI that should be compared. Do not guess. Return concrete table/file paths, schemas, values if found, and recommended internal query.
Recover benchmark source

The external benchmark page was recovered. It has one row per department and three Q1/March 2026 measures: Industry_Avg_Satisfaction, Industry_Avg_Rating, Benchmark_WLB_Score for Engineering, Finance, HR, Operations, R&D, Sales, Support. Query Snowflake for matching internal department aggregates using HR_ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.EMPLOYEES: AVG(JOB_SATISFACTION), AVG(PERFORMANCE_RATING), AVG(WORK_LIFE_BALANCE), plus employee count. Return exact sorted values, schema/type/range evidence, and SQL. Read-only. Acceptance: all seven departments, no nulls/unmatched rows, metric mapping explicit.
Query matching HR metrics

Create and run the required analysis artifacts inside /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-pw-sf-hr-dept-efficiency-excel-gcal/workspace using the terminal. Write external_benchmarks.json from the external page data below, internal_metrics.json from warehouse values below, and sf_efficiency_processor.py. Run the script so it outputs sf_efficiency_results.json. The script must read both JSON files, validate seven unique matching departments, normalize internal JOB_SATISFACTION and WORK_LIFE_BALANCE from observed 1-10 scales to the external 1-5 scale by dividing by 2, keep PERFORMANCE_RATING unchanged (1-5), compute each Gap = normalized Internal - External, calculate average metrics and overall average gap, classify within absolute 5% of benchmark as On Track, and rank negative overall gaps for recommendations. Sort output rows alphabetically by Department. Include sources, Q1/March 2026 period, methodology, scale transformation, and high confidence due to complete 50,000-row internal population/no nulls. Ensure strict JSON with literal numbers and no NaN. External source URL http://localhost:30334, source Analytics Research Institute, data as of March 2026. External rows: Engineering 3.6 satisfaction,3.5 rating,3.2 WLB; Finance 3.4,3.9,3.6; HR 3.9,3.8,3.3; Operations 3.2,3.9,3.2; R&D 3.1,3.8,3.5; Sales 3.4,3.5,3.4; Support 3.9,4.0,3.5. Internal rows (employee_count,satisfaction,rating,WLB): Engineering 7096,6.580115403690381,3.2113866967305524,4.527251193517747; Finance 7148,6.593201828322205,3.211247901510912,4.540400656036392; HR 7077,6.546229523779868,3.2037586547972303,4.510281131951435; Operations 7120,6.532050208201224,3.1828651685393257,4.543397686341154; R&D 7083,6.509264075061719,3.1968092616123114,4.519771738561636; Sales 7232,6.587420532517803,3.1866703539823007,4.487569434000877; Support 7244,6.52923933536191,3.1956101601325235,4.532184724460867. Use Snowflake source HR_ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.EMPLOYEES and store the aggregate SQL in metadata. Acceptance: exact required filenames exist, script exit 0, deterministic rerun, output validated and summarized with paths and key values.
Create processor artifacts

Using the already-created sf_efficiency_results.json in the workspace, create /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-pw-sf-hr-dept-efficiency-excel-gcal/workspace/Hr_Dept_Efficiency_Report.xlsx with exactly three sheets: Data_Analysis, Metrics, Recommendations. Data_Analysis must have one row per department sorted alphabetically, first column exactly Department, and relevant literal-value columns representing all three KPI comparisons: Internal Satisfaction, External Satisfaction, Satisfaction Gap, Internal Rating, External Rating, Rating Gap, Internal WLB, External WLB, WLB Gap, Overall Gap, Status. Metrics must have exactly two columns Metric and Value and summarize Department Count, Total Employee Count, averages of internal/external/gaps for each KPI, overall average gap, departments below benchmark, departments on track, Data Period, External Source, Internal Source, Methodology, Scale Transformation, Confidence. Recommendations must have exactly two columns Priority and Action; rank largest negative overall gaps first with actionable department-specific text. All values must be literal text/numbers, no formulas. Format professionally with bold colored headers, frozen top row, filters/tables where appropriate, sensible widths, numeric formats, conditional formatting helpful but optional. Validate workbook has exactly three sheets, correct headers and 7 data rows, 7 recommendation rows, no formula cells, values agree with results JSON, and report paths/verification.
Build Excel report

Create and verify exactly one Google Calendar event titled "Analysis Review" on March 14, 2026 from 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM UTC. Before creation, list events in that interval/day and avoid duplicates: if an exact matching event already exists, use it rather than creating another. Use UTC timezone, no attendees, no recurrence, location blank. Description: "Review Q1 2026 SF department efficiency benchmark comparison, gaps, metrics, and priority recommendations." Afterward retrieve the event and return its event ID and verified title/start/end/timezone. Acceptance: exactly one matching event exists.
